STORY
The wooden floor creaks when Amy wipes a polished table with a cloth soaked in ale‑scented oil.  
She wears a rough‑spun tunic and a leather apron that show the scuffs of her medieval trade.  

A goblin with green skin leans over the counter, its tiny hands clutching a chipped mug; Amy refills it from a barrel beside the hearth by lifting the mug and pouring ale into it.  

A beautiful female elf steps in, silver hair streaming down its shoulders, takes a seat at the back table; Amy pours a steaming cup into a crystal chalice for the elf, sets the chalice gently on the wood with a nod of thanks.  

From the doorway a dragon‑shaped creature slides onto a high bar stool; scales glitter like polished obsidian and wings unfurl to reveal amber eyes that scan the room.  
Amy greets the newcomer with a warm smile and lifts a crystal cup from her shelf, pours a special brew into it, then hands it over.  

The dragon licks its lips, takes a slow sip, letting liquid swirl across its tongue; Amy watches as the creature exhales contentedly. She wipes the bar with a fresh cloth, smoothing out any drips of ale that have fallen onto the wood.  

Finally Amy turns off lanterns at each table and pulls a wooden latch on the back door.  
She steps outside to close it, locking the tavern for the night as the moon rises over the medieval town.

generic group label when the listed identities matter to the visible event.

result or consequence, the current beat must stop before it.

story event naturally; Subject identity is resolved later from the staged RAW scene.

FULL STORY
The wooden floor creaks when Amy wipes a polished table with a cloth soaked in ale‑scented oil.  
She wears a rough‑spun tunic and a leather apron that show the scuffs of her medieval trade.  

A goblin with green skin leans over the counter, its tiny hands clutching a chipped mug; Amy refills it from a barrel beside the hearth by lifting the mug and pouring ale into it.  

A beautiful female elf steps in, silver hair streaming down its shoulders, takes a seat at the back table; Amy pours a steaming cup into a crystal chalice for the elf, sets the chalice gently on the wood with a nod of thanks.  

From the doorway a dragon‑shaped creature slides onto a high bar stool; scales glitter like polished obsidian and wings unfurl to reveal amber eyes that scan the room.  
Amy greets the newcomer with a warm smile and lifts a crystal cup from her shelf, pours a special brew into it, then hands it over.  

The dragon licks its lips, takes a slow sip, letting liquid swirl across its tongue; Amy watches as the creature exhales contentedly. She wipes the bar with a fresh cloth, smoothing out any drips of ale that have fallen onto the wood.  

Finally Amy turns off lanterns at each table and pulls a wooden latch on the back door.  
She steps outside to close it, locking the tavern for the night as the moon rises over the medieval town.

The Oak Hearth Tavern is a rectangular space measuring twenty‑two feet wide from east to west and thirty‑five feet long from south to north. The floor consists of creaking oak planks that span the entire room. On the south wall, centered, sits an entrance doorway four feet across and seven feet high, providing direct access from the street into the tavern’s interior. On the north wall near its east corner is a back door with a wooden latch three feet wide by six feet tall; it opens toward the back alley. The hearth anchors the west wall, centered between the south and north ends of that wall. It stretches six feet along the west side from east to west and extends four feet into the room. A stone base supports the creaking oak floor above it. Beside the hearth on its western edge rests a wooden barrel three feet in diameter and five feet tall. The polished wooden counter runs along the entire east wall, extending from south to north. It is two feet wide (east‑west) and one point five feet deep into the room, with a polished surface that rises up to four feet at its back edge. Halfway along this counter—seventeen point five feet north of the entrance doorway—a high bar stool sits snugly against it. The stool’s seat measures two feet square and is three feet above floor level. North of the hearth, near the back door, a single rectangular table occupies the center of the northern half of the room. It measures eight feet long by three feet wide, with four chairs arranged around its perimeter: one on each side—north, east, south, west. Above this table hangs a lantern that casts persistent light across the tavern’s interior. All objects are positioned to avoid overlap: the hearth and barrel occupy only the west wall space; the counter occupies only the east wall area without encroaching the room’s center; the back‑area table sits in the northern half, leaving clear passage from the entrance to the back door and between all seating areas. The medieval tavern ambiance is preserved with its creaking wooden floor, polished counter, stone hearth, barrel, bar stool, lanterns, and rustic furnishings.

Amy turns toward the polished wooden counter and spots a green‑skinned goblin leaning forward over its edge.

The Oak Hearth Tavern is a rectangular space measuring twenty‑two feet wide from east to west and thirty‑five feet long from south to north. The floor consists of creaking oak planks that span the entire room. On the south wall, centered, sits an entrance doorway four feet across and seven feet high, providing direct access from the street into the tavern’s interior. On the north wall near its east corner is a back door with a wooden latch three feet wide by six feet tall; it opens toward the back alley. The hearth anchors the west wall, centered between the south and north ends of that wall. It stretches six feet along the west side from east to west and extends four feet into the room. A stone base supports the creaking oak floor above it. Beside the hearth on its western edge rests a wooden barrel three feet in diameter and five feet tall. The polished wooden counter runs along the entire east wall, extending from south to north. It is two feet wide (east‑west) and one point five feet deep into the room, with a polished surface that rises up to four feet at its back edge. Halfway along this counter—seventeen point five feet north of the entrance doorway—a high bar stool sits snugly against it. The stool’s seat measures two feet square and is three feet above floor level. North of the hearth, near the back door, a single rectangular table occupies the center of the northern half of the room. It measures eight feet long by three feet wide, with four chairs arranged around its perimeter: one on each side—north, east, south, west. Above this table hangs a lantern that casts persistent light across the tavern’s interior. All objects are positioned to avoid overlap: the hearth and barrel occupy only the west wall space; the counter occupies only the east wall area without encroaching the room’s center; the back‑area table sits in the northern half, leaving clear passage from the entrance to the back door and between all seating areas. The medieval tavern ambiance is preserved with its creaking wooden floor, polished counter, stone hearth, barrel, bar stool, lanterns, and rustic furnishings.

RAW SCENE
The elf steps through the south doorway, her silver hair shimmering in the lantern light.  
She strides across the oak floor toward the back table, gliding past the chairs and bar stool with a fluid motion that takes barely 1.25 seconds from entrance to seat.  
At about  she settles onto the north-side chair of the back-table set, tucking her legs neatly beneath the narrow frame.  
She pulls up a polished wooden surface on the table—an inset tray—and places a crystal chalice upon it.  
Amy, standing beside the hearth barrel, lifts the steaming cup of ale and pours its contents into the chalice in one swift motion.  
The elf nods appreciatively as Amy sets the chalice gently on the wood, her thanks expressed with a quiet smile.

On the south wall, centered, sits an entrance doorway four feet across and seven feet high, providing direct access from the street into the tavern’s interior. The Oak Hearth Tavern is a rectangular space measuring twenty‑two feet wide from east to west and thirty‑five feet long from south to north. The floor consists of creaking oak planks that span the entire room. On the south wall, centered, sits an entrance doorway four feet across and seven feet high, providing direct access from the street into the tavern’s interior. On the north wall near its east corner is a back door with a wooden latch three feet wide by six feet tall; it opens toward the back alley. The stool’s seat measures two feet square and is three feet above floor level. North of the hearth, near the back door, a single rectangular table occupies the center of the northern half of the room. It measures eight feet long by three feet wide, with four chairs arranged around its perimeter: one on each side—north, east, south, west. Above this table hangs a lantern that casts persistent light across the tavern’s interior. All objects are positioned to avoid overlap: the hearth and barrel occupy only the west wall space; the counter occupies only the east wall area without encroaching the room’s center; the back‑area table sits in the northern half, leaving clear passage from the entrance to the back door and between all seating areas. The medieval tavern ambiance is preserved with its creaking wooden floor, polished counter, stone hearth, barrel, bar stool, lanterns, and rustic furnishings.

The Oak Hearth Tavern is a rectangular space measuring twenty‑two feet wide from east to west and thirty‑five feet long from south to north. The floor consists of creaking oak planks that span the entire room. On the south wall, centered, sits an entrance doorway four feet across and seven feet high, providing direct access from the street into the tavern’s interior. On the north wall near its east corner is a back door with a wooden latch three feet wide by six feet tall; it opens toward the back alley. The hearth anchors the west wall, centered between the south and north ends of that wall. It stretches six feet along the west side from east to west and extends four feet into the room. A stone base supports the creaking oak floor above it. Beside the hearth on its western edge rests a wooden barrel three feet in diameter and five feet tall. The polished wooden counter runs along the entire east wall, extending from south to north. It is two feet wide (east‑west) and one point five feet deep into the room, with a polished surface that rises up to four feet at its back edge. Halfway along this counter—seventeen point five feet north of the entrance doorway—a high bar stool sits snugly against it. The stool’s seat measures two feet square and is three feet above floor level. North of the hearth, near the back door, a single rectangular table occupies the center of the northern half of the room. It measures eight feet long by three feet wide, with four chairs arranged around its perimeter: one on each side—north, east, south, west. Above this table hangs a lantern that casts persistent light across the tavern’s interior. All objects are positioned to avoid overlap: the hearth and barrel occupy only the west wall space; the counter occupies only the east wall area without encroaching the room’s center; the back‑area table sits in the northern half, leaving clear passage from the entrance to the back door and between all seating areas. The medieval tavern ambiance is preserved with its creaking wooden floor, polished counter, stone hearth, barrel, bar stool, lanterns, and rustic furnishings.

STATIC SETTING AUTHORITY
The Oak Hearth Tavern is a rectangular space measuring twenty‑two feet wide from east to west and thirty‑five feet long from south to north. The floor consists of creaking oak planks that span the entire room. On the south wall, centered, sits an entrance doorway four feet across and seven feet high, providing direct access from the street into the tavern’s interior. On the north wall near its east corner is a back door with a wooden latch three feet wide by six feet tall; it opens toward the back alley. The hearth anchors the west wall, centered between the south and north ends of that wall. It stretches six feet along the west side from east to west and extends four feet into the room. A stone base supports the creaking oak floor above it. Beside the hearth on its western edge rests a wooden barrel three feet in diameter and five feet tall. The polished wooden counter runs along the entire east wall, extending from south to north. It is two feet wide (east‑west) and one point five feet deep into the room, with a polished surface that rises up to four feet at its back edge. Halfway along this counter—seventeen point five feet north of the entrance doorway—a high bar stool sits snugly against it. The stool’s seat measures two feet square and is three feet above floor level. North of the hearth, near the back door, a single rectangular table occupies the center of the northern half of the room. It measures eight feet long by three feet wide, with four chairs arranged around its perimeter: one on each side—north, east, south, west. Above this table hangs a lantern that casts persistent light across the tavern’s interior. All objects are positioned to avoid overlap: the hearth and barrel occupy only the west wall space; the counter occupies only the east wall area without encroaching the room’s center; the back‑area table sits in the northern half, leaving clear passage from the entrance to the back door and between all seating areas. The medieval tavern ambiance is preserved with its creaking wooden floor, polished counter, stone hearth, barrel, bar stool, lanterns, and rustic furnishings.

RAW SCENE
The dragon lifts its head slightly and licks its lips, amber eyes glinting in the hearth light.  
It dips a slow tongue into the swirling liquid inside the crystal cup, letting droplets glide over its tongue before swallowing slowly.  
A contented exhale rumbles from the dragon as it watches Amy's reaction.  
Amy watches intently while the liquid swirls around his tongue and he takes that slow sip.  

The dragon then lifts a freshly cleaned cloth from its own pouch, pulls it out with one hand, and wipes the polished bar smooth of any ale drips on the wood.
